mainTopic: גרם כיבוי and indirect action on שבת: candles near doors, the barrier of vessels, and ה׳'s name written on the skin
overview: The גמרא first shows that an earlier lenient ruling follows רבי שמעון בן ננס, who permits גרם כיבוי. It proves this from רבי יוסי's dissent in the משנה. Next come two ברייתות about a candle that might go out. A candle on a board may be shaken off, but only if it was forgotten there. Otherwise the board is a בסיס לדבר האסור. רב cursed the ruling allowing a door to be opened with a candle behind it, because that is a פסיק רישיה, which even רבי שמעון forbids. רב יהודה and אביי argue about opening a door opposite a fire, and their argument turns on whether to make a גזירה. The גמרא then settles which side forbids גרם כיבוי by reading a ברייתא as missing words. It also resolves a contradiction from the case of ה׳'s name written on the skin: the reed there is about not standing undressed before the name, and the argument narrows to whether one must search for a reed. The explanation of the רבנן's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The lenient ruling follows רבי שמעון בן ננס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the earlier lenient statement follows the view of רבי שמעון בן ננס in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was he (רב) who said his ruling according to רבי שמעון בן ננס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question by saying the lenient ruling was said according to רבי שמעון בן ננס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier statement allowed doing something that indirectly makes a fire go out. The גמרא explains that this is not everyone's view. It matches the view of רבי שמעון בן ננס in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of רבי שמעון בן ננס
It was he who said it

phrases.aramaic: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס.
phrases.english: It was he who said it according to Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas.
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב, and this goes back to his lenient ruling from earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised on the previous amud about the source of the lenient ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a specific תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ruling matches רבי שמעון בן ננס.

steps.title: Did רבי שמעון בן ננס really allow indirect extinguishing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רבי שמעון בן ננס only gave the reason 'it only singes.' That is not the same as permitting גרם כיבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that רבי שמעון בן ננס said 'because it only singes.' But did he say that גרם כיבוי is allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 1. It argues that רבי שמעון בן ננס's reason was about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון בן ננס allows spreading a goat's hide over a burning chest because the hide only singes and does not burn. That reason is about the hide not catching fire. It says nothing about permitting an act that causes the fire to go out, so the attribution seems unproven.

keyTerms.meaning: Indirectly causing a fire to go out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'it singes' (the hide does not burn) with 'it extinguishes' (the fire goes out). The question is whether permission for the first also implies permission for the second.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס
phrases.english: Say that Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas said
'because it only singes,'
phrases.notes: Quoting his reason in the משנה about the goat's hide.

phrases.english: did he say that indirectly causing extinguishing is permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the lenient ruling follows רבי שמעון בן ננס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His stated reason (the hide only singes) does not show he permits גרם כיבוי.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי's dissent
steps.stepSummary: Yes. רבי יוסי forbids walls of new clay jugs full of water because they will burst and put the fire out. This implies the תנא קמא (רבי שמעון בן ננס) permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. We know this because the end of the משנה teaches: רבי יוסי forbids using new clay vessels filled with water, because they cannot withstand the fire and will burst and put it out. This shows that the first תנא permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes' and proves it from the last part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי forbids the water-filled clay jugs only because they will cause the fire to go out, which is גרם כיבוי. Since he is arguing, the first opinion (רבי שמעון בן ננס) must allow it. So רבי שמעון בן ננס does permit גרם כיבוי, and the attribution in step 1 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן ננס permits גרם כיבוי. We learn this from רבי יוסי, who argues and forbids water-filled clay jugs that will burst and put out the fire.

phrases.english: Yes, since the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Yosei prohibits
new earthenware vessels full of water,
phrases.notes: Used as a barrier to stop the fire from spreading.

phrases.english: because they cannot withstand the fire
and they burst and extinguish the fire —
by inference, the first tanna permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 with a proof from the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן ננס only spoke about the hide singing, not about extinguishing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since רבי יוסי forbids because of גרם כיבוי, the תנא קמא must permit it.

steps.title: A candle on a board: shake it off
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a candle is on a board, one may shake the board so the candle falls. If it goes out, it goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if a candle is on top of a board, one shakes the board and the candle falls off. If it goes out, it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about moving a board that has a lit candle on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The candle is מוקצה, but one may shake the board to get the candle off. If the candle happens to go out from the fall, that is not a problem, because the person did not intend it.

keyTerms.meaning: If it goes out, it goes out (no concern)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נֵר שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי טַבְלָא —
phrases.english: The Sages taught: a candle that is on top of a board —
one shakes the board and it (the candle) falls,
and if it goes out — it goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נֵר שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי טַבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic: an act that might cause a candle to go out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may shake a board to drop a candle off it, even if the candle may go out.

steps.title: Only if the candle was forgotten there
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי limit the ברייתא to a case where the candle was forgotten on the board. If it was placed there on purpose, the board became a בסיס לדבר האסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: this was taught only when one forgot the candle there. But if one put it there on purpose, the board becomes a base for a forbidden object.
steps.whatsHappening: דבי רבי ינאי narrow the ברייתא from step 4 to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone deliberately left the candle on the board when שבת began, the board takes on the candle's מוקצה status. It becomes a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved at all. Only if the candle was forgotten there may one shake the board.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
A base for a forbidden (מוקצה) object

steps.whatToRemember: Shaking off the candle is allowed only if it was forgotten on the board. If it was placed there on purpose, the board is a בסיס לדבר האסור and may not be moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the הלכה of בסיס לדבר האסור: what you intentionally set an object on at the start of שבת shares its מוקצה status.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
they taught this only in a case of one who forgets,
but in a case of one who places it —
it becomes a base for a forbidden object.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּשׁוֹכֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency applies only when the candle was forgotten. A candle placed deliberately makes the board a בסיס לדבר האסור.

steps.title: A candle behind a door
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא teaches that one may open and close a door normally even if a candle is behind it. If it goes out, it goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if a candle is behind a door, one may open and close the door normally. If it goes out, it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא about a candle that might be blown out by a normal action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening the door may create a draft that puts out the candle. The ברייתא allows it anyway, because the person does not intend to put out the candle. This is the approach of דבר שאין מתכוין מותר.

phrases.english: It was taught: a candle that is behind the door —
one opens and closes it in his usual way,
and if it goes out — it goes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling to step 4, now about a door.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may open and close a door normally even though a candle behind it may go out.

steps.title: רב cursed this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב reacted to the door ruling by cursing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב cursed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports רב's very strong negative reaction to the door ruling. This sets up the question of why he did so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cursing is much stronger than simply disagreeing. That raises an obvious question about what bothered רב so much, which the גמרא asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Cursed it / spoke harshly against it

phrases.english: Rav cursed it.
phrases.notes: 'It' could mean the teaching itself or the person who acts on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts strongly against the ruling in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב strongly opposed the leniency of opening a door near a candle.

steps.title: Why did רב curse it?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asked רב אחא בריה דרבא (or רב אחא asked רב אשי) for the reason behind רב's curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אחא son of רבא (some say רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי): What is the reason רב cursed it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's curse. This sets up a series of possible explanations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא records two versions of who asked whom. The real question is the same either way: what made this ruling deserve a curse rather than a normal disagreement?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Aḥa son of Rava,
and some say

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
What is the reason Rav cursed it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב used a curse against the door ruling.

steps.title: First suggestion: רב follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב holds like רבי יהודה (דבר שאין מתכוין is forbidden), while the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because רב holds like רבי יהודה, and the תנא taught it like רבי שמעון...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes a first possible reason for the curse, and is about to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids an unintended act that may cause a מלאכה (דבר שאין מתכוין). רבי שמעון permits it. The door ruling follows רבי שמעון, so maybe רב cursed it because he follows רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion likely to be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: אילימא almost always signals a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject. Do not treat it as the final answer.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: If you say it is because Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה holds that דבר שאין מתכוין (something you didn't intend) is forbidden.

phrases.english: and the tanna taught it like Rabbi Shimon.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון holds that דבר שאין מתכוין (something you didn't intend) is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב follows רבי יהודה against the ברייתא, which follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: You don't curse a legitimate opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Holding like רבי יהודה is no reason to curse everyone who teaches like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because רב holds like רבי יהודה, would he curse everyone who teaches like רבי שמעון?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion as unreasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is a legitimate תנא, and following him is a valid opinion. A simple disagreement between תנאים cannot explain a curse. So the reason for רב's curse must be something else, which the גמרא will look for next.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Because Rav holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the suggestion in order to reject it.

phrases.english: anyone who teaches like Rabbi Shimon
he would curse him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כׇּל דְּתָנֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מֵילָט לָיֵיט לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רב's curse came from a simple מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A curse is far too harsh a response to someone who follows a legitimate תנא.

steps.title: Why רב cursed: even רבי שמעון agrees when the result is certain
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for רב's curse is that the candle will certainly go out. In a case of פסיק רישיה, even רבי שמעון forbids the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In this case even רבי שמעון agrees that it is forbidden. אביי and רבא both said that רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first explanation, the גמרא gives the real reason רב cursed the door ruling. Opening the door will definitely put out the candle, and in such a case even רבי שמעון forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון permits a דבר שאין מתכוין only when the forbidden result might not happen. When the result is certain (פסיק רישיה), he agrees it is forbidden. So the ברייתא that allowed opening the door goes against everyone, and that is why רב cursed it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cut off its head and will it not die?': an unintended result that is certain to happen

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון permits a דבר שאין מתכוין only when the result is not certain. In a פסיק רישיה case he agrees it is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון permits every unintended act. If the forbidden result is guaranteed, he forbids it too.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of פסיק רישיה is one of the most important principles in all of הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: In this case
even Rabbi Shimon agrees.
For Abaye and Rava
both said:
Rabbi Shimon agrees
in a case of 'cut off its head, and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: Meaning the forbidden result is unavoidable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 10 with a correct one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רב curse the door ruling?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The candle will certainly go out, which is a פסיק רישיה, and that is forbidden even according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב יהודה permits opening a door opposite a fire
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person may open a door facing a fire on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A person may open a door opposite a fire on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, similar ruling: opening a door when a fire is burning across from it. This sets up the reaction and discussion that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the wind coming in might fan the fire or put it out. רב יהודה is not concerned and permits it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A person may open a door
opposite a fire on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: פּוֹתֵחַ אָדָם דֶּלֶת כְּנֶגֶד מְדוּרָה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to the door and candle discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening a door opposite a fire on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: אביי curses this ruling
steps.stepSummary: אביי cursed anyone who followed רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי cursed it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי strongly objects to רב יהודה's ruling and curses it. This sets up the question of what exactly they disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors רב's curse of the door and candle ruling. A curse shows that אביי sees the leniency as seriously wrong.

phrases.english: Abaye cursed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaction against step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי forbids opening the door and condemns the leniency.

steps.title: What kind of wind are we talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case they are discussing. With a normal wind, why would anyone forbid it? With an unusual wind, why would anyone permit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If it is a normal wind, what is the reason of the one who forbids? If it is an unusual wind, what is the reason of the one who permits?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to define the case so it can understand how רב יהודה and אביי could disagree. Either option makes one of their opinions hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal wind will not affect the fire, so forbidding seems pointless. A strong, unusual wind will affect it, so permitting seems wrong. The question pushes toward a more subtle answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?
If you say with a normal wind —
what is the reason of the one who forbids?!
If with an unusual wind —
what is the reason of the one who permits?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the dispute between steps 12 and 13 is possible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of wind is the case about, so that both opinions make sense?

steps.title: A normal wind: they argue about making a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: The case is a normal wind. אביי makes a גזירה because of an unusual wind, and רב יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is a normal wind. One Sage holds that we make a decree, and the other Sage holds that we do not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is a normal wind. The argument is about whether the רבנן forbade this out of concern that a person will open the door on a day with an unusual wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a normal wind causes no actual problem. אביי worries people will confuse it with a day of strong wind, so he forbids it. רב יהודה does not make that גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a protective rabbinic decree

phrases.english: Actually, it is with a normal wind:
one master holds we make a decree,
and the other master holds we do not make a decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a normal wind, and the dispute is whether to make a גזירה because of an unusual wind.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה and אביי agree a normal wind is harmless. They argue only about making a גזירה.

steps.title: Contradiction: who forbids indirect extinguishing?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה makes it look like רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי and the רבנן permit it. A ברייתא shows the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'One may make a barrier.' Does this mean the רבנן hold that causing indirect extinguishing is permitted and רבי יוסי holds it is forbidden? But we heard the opposite from them, as a ברייתא teaches: One may make a barrier with empty vessels, and with full vessels that usually do not break. These are the full vessels that usually do not break: metal vessels. רבי יוסי says: Even vessels of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה usually do not break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about building a barrier of vessels filled with water to stop a fire. It points out that a ברייתא seems to reverse the opinions of the רבנן and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן allow all vessels, even clay ones that will burst and put out the fire, and רבי יוסי forbids new clay vessels. In the ברייתא, the רבנן allow only unbreakable metal vessels, and רבי יוסי adds certain clay vessels. So in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי is the more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: A village known for strong clay pottery

phrases.english: 'One may make a barrier,' etc.
Is this to say that the Rabbis hold
indirect extinguishing is permitted,
and Rabbi Yosei holds
indirect extinguishing is forbidden?
But we heard the opposite from them.
As it was taught: One may make a barrier
with empty vessels,
and with full ones that usually do not break.
And these are the full ones
that usually do not break —
metal vessels.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Even vessels of Kfar Shichin
and vessels of Kfar Chananya
usually do not break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's case of a barrier against fire.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of the רבנן and רבי יוסי on גרם כיבוי as shown in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, the רבנן are stricter and רבי יוסי is more lenient, which is the reverse of the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: In the ברייתא, the 'full vessels that do not break' rule means the רבנן there FORBID vessels that will break, which is the opposite of how they rule in the משנה.

steps.title: Suggestion: reverse the names in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps we should switch the opinions in the משנה. רבי יוסי in the ברייתא is only speaking according to the רבנן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Reverse the משנה, and רבי יוסי in the ברייתא is speaking according to their view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible fix: switch the names in the משנה so that the רבנן forbid and רבי יוסי permits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Then רבי יוסי really permits all vessels. In the ברייתא he is only telling the רבנן: 'Even by your own strict view, these strong clay vessels should be allowed.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a proposed answer)
He is speaking according to their view

phrases.english: And if you say: Reverse the Mishnah,
and Rabbi Yosei of the baraita
is speaking according to their view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposed answer to the contradiction of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the attribution in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows רבי יוסי as the strict one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Switch the names. רבי יוסי really permits, and in the ברייתא he argues according to the רבנן's view.

steps.title: You cannot reverse it: רב says רבי יוסי forbids
steps.stepSummary: Reversing the משנה is impossible because רב said that רבי יוסי is the תנא who forbids גרם כיבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can you reverse it? רבה בר תחליפא said in the name of רב: Who is the תנא who says indirect extinguishing is forbidden? רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea of switching the names. An אמורא's tradition clearly says רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's statement fits the משנה as it is written, where רבי יוסי is strict. So the משנה cannot be reversed, and the contradiction with the ברייתא is back.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught

phrases.english: But can you reverse it?
But Rabba bar Tachlifa said
in the name of Rav:
Who is the tanna who holds indirect extinguishing is forbidden —
Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reversal proposed in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire suggestion to switch the names in the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's tradition confirms that רבי יוסי is the one who forbids גרם כיבוי, as the משנה is written.

steps.title: Final answer: the whole ברייתא is רבי יוסי, with missing words
steps.stepSummary: Do not reverse the משנה. The whole ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, and it is missing words. The clay vessels of שיחין and חנניה are allowed because they are strong and do not break.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, do not reverse it. The whole ברייתא is רבי יוסי, and it is missing words and teaches like this: One may make a barrier with empty vessels and with full vessels that usually do not break. These are the vessels that usually do not break: metal vessels. Vessels of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה also usually do not break, as רבי יוסי says: Even vessels of כפר שיחין and כפר חנניה usually do not break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final resolution. The משנה stays as is, and the ברייתא is read as one statement of רבי יוסי with a few words added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי forbids vessels that will break and put out the fire, since that is גרם כיבוי. The clay vessels of שיחין and חנניה are so strong that they do not break, so even he allows them. There is no 'lenient רבי יוסי' against 'strict רבנן' in the ברייתא at all, so the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is how it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה stays as written: רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי. The ברייתא is entirely his view, and it only adds that strong clay vessels from שיחין and חנניה count as unbreakable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב's rule that רבי יוסי is the תנא who forbids גרם כיבוי, and it shows the common tool of חסורי מחסרא for fixing a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rather, actually, do not reverse it,
and the entire baraita is Rabbi Yosei.
And it is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
One may make a barrier with empty vessels
and with full ones that usually do not break.
And these are the vessels
that usually do not break: metal vessels.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְלֵי כְּפַר שִׁיחִין וּכְלֵי כְּפַר חֲנַנְיָה
phrases.english: And vessels of Kfar Shichin and vessels of Kfar Chananya
also usually do not break,
for Rabbi Yosei says:
Even vessels of Kfar Shichin
and vessels of Kfar Chananya
usually do not break.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the contradiction of step 16 after the reversal in step 17 was rejected in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מחסרא: rereading the ברייתא as a single opinion with missing words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows the רבנן as strict and רבי יוסי as lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole ברייתא is רבי יוסי. He forbids breakable vessels and only adds that the strong clay vessels of שיחין and חנניה count as unbreakable.

steps.title: A new contradiction from the case of ה׳'s name written on the skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets each side against itself. In our משנה the רבנן are lenient about indirect action and רבי יוסי is strict. In a ברייתא about ה׳'s name written on a person's skin, the רבנן are strict and רבי יוסי is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of the רבנן, and between two statements of רבי יוסי. A ברייתא teaches: if a person has ה׳'s name written on his skin, he may not wash, may not smear oil, and may not stand in a dirty place. If he needs a טבילה של מצוה, he wraps a reed over the name and then goes down and immerses. רבי יוסי says he may always go down and immerse in his normal way, as long as he does not rub the spot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to flip both opinions. The רבנן look strict about indirect erasure, and רבי יוסי looks lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing in water does not directly erase the name, but the water might wash it away. That is an indirect result. The רבנן require covering the name with a reed, which is strict about indirect action, while רבי יוסי allows normal immersion as long as he does not rub. This is the reverse of their positions on גרם כיבוי in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets one source against another. This is the language of pointing out a contradiction.
Here it means ה׳'s holy name, which may not be erased.
An immersion that is required for a מצוה, such as becoming טהור
A reed. It is wrapped around the name to protect it from the water.
He rubs. Rubbing would erase the name directly.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get mixed up about who is strict here. In this ברייתא it is the רבנן who are strict about indirect erasure, because they require the reed. רבי יוסי is the lenient one. That flip is exactly the problem the גמרא is raising.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis,
and he raised a contradiction between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yosei.
As it was taught: if there was a name of God
written on his skin,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִרְחוֹץ וְלֹא יָסוּךְ
phrases.english: he may not wash and he may not smear oil,
phrases.notes: Either action might erase the name.

phrases.english: and he may not stand in a filthy place.
phrases.notes: This would be disrespectful to ה׳'s name.

phrases.english: If a מצוה immersion came his way,
he wraps a reed over it, and goes down and immerses.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם יוֹרֵד וְטוֹבֵל כְּדַרְכּוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he may always go down and immerse in his usual way,
as long as he does not rub!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן, וְרָמֵי דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once the opinions in the משנה are settled (רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי and the רבנן permit it), a different ברייתא is used to challenge both sides for being inconsistent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both the רבנן and רבי יוסי on the topic of indirect causation (גרמא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן are lenient about indirect extinguishing but strict about indirect erasure. רבי יוסי is strict about indirect extinguishing but lenient about indirect erasure. Each side seems to contradict itself.

steps.title: A פסוק permits indirect erasure of ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי. With ה׳'s name, the Torah's wording 'do not do so' forbids only direct action, so indirect erasure is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the פסוק says: 'And you shall destroy their name from that place. You shall not do so to ה׳ your God.' Only doing it directly is forbidden. Causing it indirectly is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבי יוסי. It says the case of ה׳'s name has a special source in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition of erasing ה׳'s name comes from the words 'לא תעשון כן', meaning 'do not do so'. The word 'do' implies that only a direct action is forbidden, so indirect erasure (גרמא) is allowed. That is why רבי יוסי can be lenient there even though he forbids גרם כיבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. The case being compared has its own special reason.
'And you shall destroy their name.' This is said about idols, and the next פסוק teaches not to do the same to ה׳'s name.
Doing something directly with your own action

phrases.english: It is different there, because the verse says:
"And you shall destroy their name from that place,
you shall not do so to the Lord your God":
doing it is what is forbidden; causing it indirectly is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the רבי יוסי half of the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the erasure case has its own פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי had one general view about indirect action that should apply to every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: For ה׳'s name, the wording 'do not do' limits the prohibition to direct action. That is why רבי יוסי allows indirect erasure there.

steps.title: The same wording appears for מלאכה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The Torah also says 'do not do any מלאכה' on שבת, so indirect extinguishing should be allowed there too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, here too it is written: 'Do not do any מלאכה.' Only doing it directly should be forbidden, and causing it indirectly should be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It points out that the same kind of wording, 'do', appears in the prohibition of מלאכה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word 'do' limits the erasure prohibition to direct action, it should also limit מלאכה on שבת to direct action. Then רבי יוסי should permit גרם כיבוי, yet in our משנה he forbids it. So the contradiction in רבי יוסי seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. This introduces a challenge based on what was just said.
A forbidden creative act on שבת

phrases.english: If so, here too it is written:
"You shall not do any labor":
doing it is what is forbidden; causing it indirectly should be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the answer from step 21 by applying the same reasoning to שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 21, and רבי יוסי's ban on גרם כיבוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording in the שבת prohibition is the same kind of wording, 'do'. So indirect extinguishing should be allowed, which contradicts רבי יוסי in the משנה.

steps.title: A person panics over his money
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees that גרמא is permitted on the Torah level. He forbids it in a fire only because a panicked owner might end up putting out the fire directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a person panics about his money, if you permit him to put out the fire indirectly, he will come to put it out directly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי's ban on גרם כיבוי is a rabbinic safeguard (גזירה), not a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the Torah level, indirect extinguishing really is allowed, just like indirect erasure. But when a fire threatens a person's property he is upset and in a rush. If he is allowed to act indirectly, he may go further and put out the fire directly. No such worry exists with ה׳'s name.

keyTerms.meaning: Panicked and anxious about his property
He will come to extinguish it directly

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea. Indirect extinguishing is allowed by Torah law, and any ban on it comes from the worry that a person will slip into a direct action.

phrases.english: Since a person is agitated about his property,
if you permit him, he will come to extinguish it directly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This defends רבי יוסי against the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the ban as a rabbinic safeguard (גזירה) because of a special worry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי forbids גרם כיבוי because it counts as מלאכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: גרמא is permitted on the Torah level. The ban applies only in a fire, because panic over money may lead to directly putting out the fire.

steps.title: The contradiction in the רבנן becomes even stronger
steps.stepSummary: If panic over money is a reason to be strict, the רבנן permit indirect extinguishing even with that worry present. Surely they should permit indirect erasure of ה׳'s name, where that worry does not exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a contradiction between the רבנן and the רבנן. In the fire case, where a person panics about his money, they still permit it. Here, with ה׳'s name, should it not be permitted all the more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the רבנן's side of the contradiction. It uses the answer it just gave to make the question against them even sharper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire case has an extra risk, because a panicked owner might extinguish directly, and still the רבנן permit גרם כיבוי. The case of ה׳'s name has no such risk. So by a קל וחומר, the רבנן should certainly allow normal immersion, yet in the ברייתא they require covering the name with a reed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. This states that there is a problem.
'And if...' This opens a קל וחומר argument.

phrases.english: If so, there is a difficulty between the Rabbis and the Rabbis:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הָתָם דְּאָדָם בָּהוּל עַל מָמוֹנוֹ — שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: if there, where a person is agitated about his property, it is permitted,
here, is it not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving רבי יוסי's side, the גמרא goes back to the רבנן's half of the contradiction from step 20. It makes that question stronger by using the reasoning from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's strict ruling in the ברייתא about immersing with ה׳'s name on the skin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a קל וחומר. If the רבנן permit indirect action where there is a risk of panic over money, they should certainly permit it where there is no such risk.

steps.title: The reed cannot be there to prevent erasure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the רבנן's reed is meant to keep the name from being erased. A tight reed blocks the water, and a loose reed lets the water reach the name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really understand it that way? What is the case of this reed? If it is tied on tightly, it is a barrier that blocks the immersion. If it is not tied tightly, the water gets in under it anyway!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the assumption behind the last question. That question assumed the רבנן care about indirect erasure, but their reed cannot be doing that job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 24 assumed the reed protects ה׳'s name from the water. Either way, though, the reed fails as protection. A tight reed is a חציצה, which ruins the טבילה, and a loose reed lets the water in, so the name gets wet anyway. That means the רבנן's reed must be there for some other reason, and the question from step 24 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a challenge to an assumption)
A reed or rush, wrapped around the name
A barrier between the body and the water, which makes an immersion invalid

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question in step 24 directly. It knocks out the assumption the question was built on, namely that the reed is about erasure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to look for a completely different reason for the רבנן's reed. That search drives the rest of this passage.

phrases.english: And can you understand it so?
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's way of saying the last question started from a wrong assumption.

phrases.english: This reed, what is its case?
If it is tight, it is a barrier;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא מִיהַדַּק — עָיְילִי בֵּיהּ מַיָּא!
phrases.english: if it is not tight, water enters under it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the premise of the challenge in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that the רבנן's reed exists to prevent indirect erasure of ה׳'s name.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A reed either blocks the water (חציצה) or fails to keep the water out, so it cannot serve as protection against erasure.

steps.title: The ink itself should already be a barrier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes a side point. If the worry is a barrier, the ink on the skin should already count as one, even without a reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you are worried about a barrier, get it from the ink! The ink itself should be a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about the reasoning just used. Why mention the reed as a barrier, when the ink of the name is already sitting on the skin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said a tight reed would be a חציצה. But the letters are written in ink on the person's skin, and the ink is also something between the body and the water. So the immersion should be a problem anyway, with or without a reed.

keyTerms.meaning: Derive it already from (another, simpler reason)

phrases.english: As for a barrier, derive it already from the ink!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions part of the reasoning in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of חציצה in step 25 to reject the tight reed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ink on the skin would already be a חציצה, so the reed adds nothing new to the problem.

steps.title: The ink is still wet, and wet ink does not block
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the ink is still wet. A ברייתא teaches that wet substances on the skin do not count as a barrier, while dry ones do.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is with wet ink. As a ברייתא teaches: blood, ink, honey and milk, when dry, are a barrier. When wet, they are not a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question. It explains that the ink is wet and backs this up with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet substances do not count as a חציצה, while dry ones do. So wet ink causes no problem, and the only possible barrier is the tight reed. The point made in step 25 stands.

phrases.english: With moist ink.
phrases.notes: The short answer. The rest of the step is its proof.

phrases.english: As it was taught: blood, ink, honey, and milk,
when dry, they interpose;
when moist, they do not interpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side question from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ink is moist.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ink on the skin is already a חציצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist ink does not interpose, so only a tight reed would be a barrier.

steps.title: Either way, why do the רבנן need a reed?
steps.stepSummary: With the side point settled, the גמרא returns to the main problem. The reed cannot prevent erasure, so why do the רבנן require it at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult! Why do the רבנן require a reed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא comes back to the main question. The reed seems to have no purpose, so what is the רבנן's reason?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 25–27 showed that the reed cannot stop the water. So the רבנן's demand for a reed now needs a new explanation.

phrases.english: Nevertheless, it is difficult?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side issue to the main difficulty that step 25 created.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's requirement to wrap a reed around ה׳'s name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reed does not prevent erasure, so it seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The reed is there so one does not stand undressed before ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב שילא explains that the רבנן's reason has nothing to do with erasure. It is forbidden to stand undressed in front of ה׳'s name, so the name must be covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא בר רב שילא said: This is the רבנן's reason. They hold that it is forbidden to stand undressed before ה׳'s name.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב שילא gives a brand-new reason for the reed. It is about respect for ה׳'s name, not about erasure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reed does not need to keep water out. It only needs to cover the name, so the person is not standing undressed in front of it. So the reed is not a case of the רבנן being strict about indirect erasure. That removes the contradiction raised in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand in front of ה׳'s name

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's reed is about not standing undressed before ה׳'s name. It has nothing to do with erasure, so the רבנן do not contradict themselves on גרמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reason means the two sources no longer conflict for the רבנן. The rest of this passage then checks how רבי יוסי handles the same concern.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא,
phrases.english: Rather, Rava bar Rav Sheila said:
This is the reason of the Rabbis, for they hold:
It is forbidden to stand before the name naked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in step 28 with a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reed is a protection against indirect erasure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reed is a covering, so one does not stand undressed before ה׳'s name.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי allow standing undressed before ה׳'s name?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי does not require a reed. The גמרא asks whether that means he permits standing undressed in front of ה׳'s name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that רבי יוסי holds it is permitted to stand undressed before ה׳'s name?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new explanation on the other side of the argument. If the reed is about respect, what about רבי יוסי, who does not require it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument is about whether a covering is needed, then רבי יוסי seems to allow something very disrespectful. That is hard to accept.

phrases.english: By implication, Rabbi Yosei holds
it is permitted to stand before the name naked?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the explanation from step 29 against רבי יוסי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבא בר רב שילא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן need a reed for respect, then רבי יוסי, who needs no reed, would seem to permit standing undressed before ה׳'s name.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a hand over the name is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי agrees the name must be covered. He holds that placing one's hand over it is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He places his hand over it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי also forbids standing undressed before the name. He just covers it with his hand instead of a reed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the two sides do not disagree about respect for the name. They disagree only about what kind of covering is good enough.

phrases.english: He places his hand over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי allows standing undressed before the name.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי also requires a covering, but a hand is enough.

steps.title: Then the רבנן should also accept a hand
steps.stepSummary: If a hand is a good enough covering, the גמרא asks why the רבנן do not accept it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the רבנן too, let him place his hand over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the רבנן. Why insist on a reed when a hand would also cover the name?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a hand works for רבי יוסי, the רבנן's demand for a reed looks unnecessary.

phrases.english: For the Rabbis too, let him place his hand over it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer from step 31 against the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's requirement of a reed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hand is a good enough covering, so a reed should not be required.

steps.title: The רבנן fear he will forget and move his hand
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן worry that a person will sometimes forget and take his hand away, leaving the name uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he forgets and removes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן do not trust a hand. A person may forget and move it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reed stays in place without any thought, but a hand depends on the person remembering. So the רבנן want the safer covering.

phrases.english: Sometimes he forgets and removes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 32.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hand is just as good as a reed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A hand may slip off through forgetfulness, so the רבנן require a reed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי should share the same worry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי is not also worried that the person will forget and remove his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוסי too, sometimes he forgets and removes it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the רבנן's worry back on רבי יוסי. The same risk seems to apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forgetting is a normal human risk, not something tied to one opinion. So why would רבי יוסי ignore it?

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yosei too,
sometimes he forgets and removes it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer in step 33 to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's acceptance of a hand as a covering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worry about forgetting applies to everyone, so רבי יוסי should also require a reed.

steps.title: They disagree only when a reed must be searched for
steps.stepSummary: If a reed is at hand, רבי יוסי agrees that one uses it. The argument is only about a case where one would have to go looking for a reed. This passage ends as the גמרא begins stating the רבנן's view in that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if a reed is available, רבי יוסי indeed agrees one uses it. What case are we dealing with here? Where he would have to go looking for a reed. The רבנן hold…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument to one specific case: when no reed is handy. The last words, 'the רבנן hold', set up the next move, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides prefer a reed and both care about the name being covered. The real question is whether one must put off the immersion to search for a reed. The reason each side gives follows right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי and the רבנן both require covering ה׳'s name and both use a reed if one is there. They argue only when a reed would have to be searched for.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי rejects the reed. He uses one when it is available. The argument is only about having to go and look for one.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִי דְּאִיכָּא גֶּמִי — הָכִי נָמֵי,
phrases.english: Rather: if there is a reed, indeed so (he uses it);
here, with what are we dealing?
with having to seek a reed.
The Rabbis hold…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִי דְּאִיכָּא גֶּמִי — הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 34 by narrowing what the argument is about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי never requires a reed, even when one is available.
steps.terutzMaskana: When a reed is available, everyone uses it. The argument is only about whether one must go searching for one.
